transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi. Well, I came in because I'm just so tired. I can barely get through a shift at work right now. It feels like my body is filled with wet sand, honestly. And, um, resting doesn't really bring me back. I just stay exhausted.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling sad, down, or depressed?

I wouldn't really say I feel sad or... or depressed. I haven't been crying or feeling down about anything in particular. Um, it's really just the exhaustion. I'm maybe a little frustrated that I'm so tired all the time and can't get my energy back, but... yeah, not really sad.
Besides the exhaustion, have you been experiencing any anxiety, worry, or nervousness that's been bothering you?

No, not really. Um, I haven't been feeling anxious or nervous about anything. Like I said, it's really just the physical tiredness. I don't sit around worrying about things, I'm just... too drained for that, I guess.
When did this exhaustion first start? Was it sudden or did it come on gradually over time?

It's been going on for about a month now. Um, it started right around the time the store changed our hours during a remodel. I guess it was pretty sudden... it just kind of hit me then, and I haven't been able to shake the tiredness since.
Have you noticed any other changes in your body recently, like weight gain, feeling cold more easily, or changes in your appetite or digestion?

Um, I haven't really noticed feeling cold or anything like that. But my appetite has been kind of... all over the place. Lately, I mostly just forget to eat, to be honest. Or when I do, the food just tastes like cardboard. I haven't gained weight, but I have noticed my work pants have been fitting a lot looser recently, so I guess I've been losing it instead.
Have you been feeling unusually cold, or noticed that you feel cold more easily than you used to before this exhaustion started?
Um, no, not really. Like I just said a minute ago, I haven't noticed feeling cold or anything like that. My temperature feels pretty normal to me.
Before this exhaustion started about a month ago, did you have any illness like a cold, flu, or infection? Or did you have any head injuries or accidents around that time?
Um, no, nothing like that. I didn't have a cold or the flu... and I definitely haven't hit my head or been in any kind of accident. I was perfectly fine right up until all this tiredness started.
Have you noticed any problems with your concentration, memory, or thinking clearly since this tiredness started? Or have you had any headaches?

Um, no, not really. I haven't had any headaches. And my memory seems fine, I think. I mean, I guess I'm a little foggy sometimes just because I'm so tired, but I haven't noticed any real problems with concentrating or thinking clearly. It's mostly just the exhaustion.
In the week or two right before the exhaustion started, did you have any symptoms like body aches, sore throat, fever, cough, or just feeling generally unwell, even if it was mild?
No, I didn't have any of that. I wasn't sick at all before this. No fever, no cough, no body aches... nothing like that. I felt completely fine, right up until the exhaustion just sort of took over.
Before this exhaustion started, were there activities or hobbies that you really enjoyed doing? And if so, do you still find those things enjoyable now, or has your interest in them changed?

Yeah, I did. I usually love cooking for myself, playing my guitar, going hiking... or just going over to my family’s place. But now... I don't know, it all just feels flat. I don't really enjoy them anymore. Even if I try to do those things, it just feels like I’m only pretending to care.
When you say those activities feel flat and you're only pretending to care, have you been feeling this way about most things in your life, or is it mainly just those hobbies?

I think it's pretty much everything. Um... yeah, it's not just my hobbies. It's just a general feeling. Like, even just going in for my shifts at the store or talking to people... it all just feels the same. I just don't really care about much of anything right now.
Are you currently taking any medications, or have you started any new medications in the past month or two? Also, do you use any drugs, alcohol, or other substances regularly?
No, I don't take any medications. I haven't started anything new either. And... no, I don't really drink or use drugs. I might have a beer like, once in a blue moon, but that's it. Nothing regular.
When the store remodel started and your hours changed, was that a particularly stressful time for you? Or did anything else significant happen in your life around that same time?

Um, I don't know if it was super stressful. It was just different, I guess. I mean, the hours changed and things got moved around, but... I don't really think it was a big deal. And no, nothing else really happened around then. Just work.

Have you had any recent lab work or medical tests done? And has your doctor checked you for things like thyroid problems, anemia, vitamin deficiencies, or any kind of infection or inflammation in the past month or so?
Um, no, I haven't had any lab work or tests done. I haven't actually been to a regular doctor in a while, so... no, nobody has checked my thyroid or vitamins or anything like that recently.
Have you noticed any other physical symptoms besides the tiredness and weight loss? For example, any fevers, night sweats, body aches, or just a general feeling of being physically unwell?

No, not really. I mean, I haven't had any fevers or night sweats or anything like that. My body doesn't ache. I just... I just feel really tired, like I said. But physically, besides that and losing some weight, I feel fine. Nothing else stands out.

You mentioned the exhaustion started when the store remodel began about a month ago. But looking back even further—in the month or two before that remodel started, did you have any kind of medical event, illness, surgery, or health problem that I should know about?

Um, no, nothing like that. Before the remodel started, everything was pretty normal. I haven't been sick, no surgeries or hospital visits or anything. Like I said, I haven't really been to a doctor in a long time, so there hasn't been any big medical stuff going on. Just work and my normal routine before all this started.
Looking back to about 5 or 6 weeks ago, before the store remodel started—do you remember being sick at all during that time, even if it was something mild that you got over quickly?
No, I don't think so. I really can't remember having a cold or a bug or anything like that. Everything was just completely normal before all the remodel stuff started at the store.

I know you said you don't remember being sick, but let me ask it a different way—in the month or two before the remodel started, did you have any period where you just didn't feel quite right, even if you didn't think it was serious enough to call it being 'sick'? Like maybe just feeling run-down, or having mild aches, or a scratchy throat, or just something being a little off for a few days?

No, honestly... I really didn't. I know you're trying to figure out if something else was going on, but I felt completely fine back then. No scratchy throat, no feeling run-down or off. Everything was just normal until the remodel started.
Even if you didn't think it was serious, did anyone around you—like coworkers, family, or friends—get sick with a cold or flu in the weeks right before the remodel started?
No, not that I can remember. I mean, nobody at work called out sick or anything, and I don't really see a lot of people outside of work. So, no, I don't think anyone around me was sick either.
In the few weeks before the remodel started, did you get any kind of test done—like for COVID, the flu, or anything else—that came back positive, even if you didn't have symptoms?
No, I didn't take any tests. Like I said, I felt fine, so there wasn't any reason to get tested for COVID or the flu or anything.
